live.note: Real providers via the Core vault, broker and TLS. Keys never stored in evidence (scanned). EXTERNAL_BLOCKED = account without funds/limit, not a pass.

scope: C1 only: optional llm_engine plugin (python3_script) with Core-held key vault, Core-brokered HTTP, cloud consent default off, streaming partials, Safety-gated tool proposals, Qt chat and engine dialog. No Model Manager, no local runtime (llama.cpp is C2), no agent loop (C3).
limitations: Live: OpenRouter (403, key limit 0) and OpenCode (402, no funds) were EXTERNAL_BLOCKED; DeepSeek (402) and ZenMux (403) were smoke-tested by hand only and are not Core providers. Only Google and Mistral produced real model output.
Mistral runs through the custom https provider (no dedicated provider id).
Model quality, tool-call reliability and latency of real providers are not measured; the live gate asserts a one-word reply and a tool request only.
No local LLM runtime yet (llama.cpp planned for C2); no Model Manager (C2, plugin-only).

host_call permission_denied is proven in Rust tests, not by the process gate (single-plugin catalog); the deadline gate does not assert plugin exit (C0 semantics); S1 during an active stream is not provable (boot replay outlasts the 10 s capability cap).
Packaged-interpreter sandbox flags (--cap-drop, tmpfs size) verified with /usr python in Rust tests and in the C0 package gate; no seccomp filter; exec of /usr binaries allowed.
Key passes through a Qt text field for one call, Qt strings cannot be zeroed.
Tool execution only through the fixed registry and the sandbox command profile; the LLM never receives tool results (agent loop is C3).
Physical audio/KDE Wayland/Flatpak not validated; publisher unauthenticated; human validation consolidated after S5.
